contradictions.detail: The listing feature list claims '18 Inch Wheels' and '20 Inch Wheels'. The listing's own photo caption and the window sticker show 19-inch Carrera Classic wheels. This is likely a generic data-feed error.
The Carfax 08/06/2026 title event notes the colour as Beige. The car is Midnight Blue Metallic per the sticker and photos. Most likely the interior colour was recorded.

critical_evidence.evidence: No borescope images or engine rebuild invoices are in the listing or the Carfax. This is a 3.4 M97, the exposed engine. Long periods of very low use (about 1,270 miles in 6.5 years) do not rule out scoring. 'Low miles' is not evidence of clean bores.

No over-rev report is provided. The 04/15/2025 Carfax entry 'Engine/powertrain computer/module checked' at Audi Porsche of Grand Rapids is not an over-rev readout. Ask for that invoice and a fresh range report.

The Carfax has no reported entry for coolant, water pump, coolant pipes, AOS, spark plugs or a major service in 20 years. Only oil, brake fluid (2010, 2016) and 'maintenance inspection' (2018, 2025) are listed. No reported entry does not prove the work was not done, but nothing documents it.

documentation.rationale: The identity half is strong: the VIN, the original window sticker, a one-owner Carfax with a steady odometer series, and a clean title. The maintenance half is thin: seven Carfax lines, mostly oil changes, with no invoices. There is nothing on cooling, AOS or water pump, no borescope and no DME report. Two oil services (2012, 2013) were at a Subaru dealer.

condition.rationale: The photos show tidy paint, unworn-looking wheels and a clean cabin, with light creasing and a scuff on the driver's outer seat bolster. Nothing mechanical is proven either way. There is no underside, engine-bay, tire-date or scan evidence. The car sat with minimal use from 2018 to 2025, which puts age items (coolant, seals, tires, AOS) in question.

price_value.rationale: The $41,995 ask sits well above the fair-value range of $30,096–$36,451 (mid $32,806). Retail dealer sales of very-low-mile S cars ($40,998 and $41,900) show the number is not unheard of. However, those buyers paid for evidence this car has not yet shown: borescope, cooling and AOS records.

mission_fit.rationale: This is a keeper-type car, which matches the future_keeper mission. However, the profile says a 3.4 S is bought only with unusually strong engine due diligence, and none is present yet. The asking price also conflicts with the current cash-preservation posture.

logistics.rationale: Massachusetts dealer, so this is a fly-and-drive or ship purchase. PPI access is not stated, though the region has Porsche specialists who could borescope it. It is a federal-emissions car above 7,500 miles, so California registration looks feasible pending smog. The dealer-held Montana title needs clarifying.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: Several desirable traits together: 6-speed manual, Midnight Blue over Sand Beige, one 20-year owner, original window sticker, low miles, Bi-Xenon and 19-inch Carrera Classics. It lacks Sport Chrono, PASM and full leather, so it falls short of a top-spec car.

what_would_change_verdict: A clean independent borescope with images plus a benign DME over-rev report would materially raise documentation and condition.
Invoices showing cooling-system, AOS and water-pump work, or a price move toward the fair-value range, would improve value.
Any scoring, metal in the filter, over-rev events in the high ranges, or a seller refusal to allow a borescope would move it sharply down.
Tires found to be old date codes would add known work.
evidence.mission_note: It fits the future_keeper brief on specification (manual, desirable colour, one owner). However, it is a 3.4 S without the engine evidence the profile requires, and it is priced above fair value. It is attractive only as a keeper, and that conflicts with the current cash-preservation posture.
evidence.rationale: The Carfax and the window-sticker photo firmly establish identity: a 2006 Cayman S, 3.4 M97, 6-speed manual, Midnight Blue over Sand Beige. It shows one retail owner for 20 years, a clean title, no reported accidents and a consistent odometer at 35,612. Maintenance evidence is limited to seven Carfax lines, mostly oil changes and inspections at Porsche dealers. Two oil changes were done at a Subaru dealer, and brake fluid was changed in 2010 and 2016. There is no reported entry for coolant, water pump, AOS, plugs or clutch in two decades. The car saw very little use from 2018 to 2025, with no reported oil-change entry between 2016 and 2025. Nothing mechanically wrong is observed. The photos show a clean exterior and cabin with minor bolster wear, but no underside, engine bay or tire dates are examined here. All three model-critical items for this bore-scoring-exposed engine are missing: the borescope, the DME over-rev report and cooling/AOS documentation. The $41,995 ask sits above the fair-value range of $30,096–$36,451.
evidence.next_action: Ask the dealer in writing for PPI access with an independent Porsche specialist (borescope with images, DME over-rev report, scan), plus the 2025 Grand Rapids invoice and tire date codes, before discussing price or paying any deposit.
